subject: Reserved commit term & ramp schedule for Dedicated capacity — EdgeScale
messages:
From: Maya Liu <maya.liu@edgescale.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity — initial ask and timing

Hi Karthik,

We ran your Dedicated capacity benchmark last week and it looks promising. We're planning a pilot to back our new chat + retrieval product and have an initial sizing ask: ~8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (sustained), with bursts up to 12 for launches.

Key questions from procurement and engineering:
- Pricing by reserved commit term (12 / 24 / 36 months) and expected discount tiers
- How you handle the ramp schedule (we don't need full 8 GPUs day 1; want a 3–6 month ramp)
- Capacity start date flexibility — we have a compliance blackout in mid-April and would prefer capacity to start May 1
- Throughput guarantees / SLOs for tail latency at 95th percentile (we publish internal SLOs to customers)

Can you share an initial proposal or a spreadsheet we can review? Procurement included on this thread (procurement@edgescale.com).

Thanks —
Maya
Maya Liu
Head of Platform
EdgeScale Inc.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maya Liu <maya.liu@edgescale.com>, procurement <procurement@edgescale.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial ask and timing

Hi Maya — thanks for the details and for running the benchmark. Looping in Monica (solutions) — she'll help map the ramp and SLOs.

High-level on commit terms and discounts (ballpark numbers to start):
- 12-month reserved commit: baseline pricing, 8–12% discount to on-demand Dedicated rates
- 24-month reserved commit: ~15–22% discount (depends on avg sustained utilization in year 1)
- 36-month reserved commit: up to 28% discount with locked pricing and optional renewal credits

Notes / assumptions:
- Discounts assume you commit to a steady-state equivalent of 8 GPUs; if effective sustained usage is <60% we factor a utilization adjustment
- Burst capacity (12 GPUs) is supported via a configurable burst pool; bursts billed at reduced premium vs on-demand but not counted toward commit baseline unless you opt-in

Attachments: I attached a draft pricing spreadsheet and a proposed ramp schedule (commit_schedule.xlsx) and a narrative pricing PDF (redwood_dedicated_pricing_v3.pdf).

Question for procurement: do you have internal approval guardrails for multi-year contracts? Monica / finance (cc laura) — should we show an alternative phased-payment schedule?

Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: commit_schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet)] [Attachment: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v3.pdf (pdf)]

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Maya Liu <maya.liu@edgescale.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, procurement <procurement@edgescale.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial ask and timing

Maya — quick follow on from the solutions side with a concrete ramp option that matches your description:

Proposed ramp (example):
- Month 0 (onboarding, staging): 2 GPUs available for testing + KV cache priming
- Month 1: scale to 4 GPUs sustained, bursts to 6 during release windows
- Month 3: scale to 8 GPUs sustained (full commit baseline)
- Month 6: optional expansion to 10–12 GPUs based on negotiated burst-to-commit conversion

Throughput / SLOs: we can offer a 95th percentile latency SLO at the route level (for your configured model + seq length) with a financial credit construct tied to missed SLOs. Typical language: 99% availability on the reserved pool and 95th percentile latency target for warm requests (cache primed) — we will run a joint test plan to map the exact numbers into the contract.

Operational notes:
- We recommend a target capacity start date of May 1 to accommodate your compliance blackout. That gives us 6 weeks for onboarding and canary runs.
- If you need earlier pilot capacity, we can provide a short-term burst pool (billed at a small premium) that doesn't impact the reserved commit start date.

I'll drop a version of the ramp schedule into the spreadsheet with these milestones.

—Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Maya Liu <maya.liu@edgescale.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement <procurement@edgescale.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Mar 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial ask and timing

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement asked for two clarifications before we can move to internal approvals:

1) Discount variability: can you provide a firm price table for the three terms with both a committed baseline of 8 GPUs and a conservative baseline of 6 GPUs? They want to see the delta if our sustained usage is lower.
2) Capacity start date: May 1 works for us. However, if we sign in late March can you commit to that start date and guarantee the onboarding timeline? Procurement wants language that the reserved pool will be available and that canary windows finish before our public launch (no less than two weeks prior).

We also wanted to push on discount a bit — our procurement target is in the low 20s for a 24-month deal if we can commit to the 8-GPU baseline and a 6-month ramp. Is that something Redwood can consider?

Maya

Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial ask and timing

Maya / procurement,

Thanks for the clarity — answer below and next steps.

1) Firm price table: attached spreadsheet includes a two-scenario table (6 GPU baseline vs 8 GPU baseline) across 12/24/36 months. Summary:
- 12 month (8 GPU baseline): standard discount ~10%
- 24 month (8 GPU baseline): 20% discount (we can commit to a firm 20% if you accept the 6-month ramp to full 8 GPUs)
- 36 month (8 GPU baseline): 26% discount with a price lock and optional usage credits at renewal

For a 6 GPU baseline the discounts come down ~3–5 percentage points across terms in the attached. See commit_schedule.xlsx for the full breakdown.

2) Capacity start date and onboarding guarantee: if we execute the MSA and SOW by March 25, Redwood will prioritize onboarding and commit to a pool available on May 1. We'll include a canary run window and acceptance criteria in the SOW — if onboarding runs late (outside of vendor-caused delay) the contract will include a service credit tied to missed milestones.

3) Pricing concession: we can meet your procurement target of low-20s on a 24-month term (firm 20% discount today) if you: (a) sign by March 25, and (b) accept the 6-month ramp schedule to full 8 GPU sustained baseline. We will add a clause that allows you to convert up to 2 GPUs of burst into committed capacity at pre-agreed pricing during months 6–12.

Next steps:
- I'll route a draft SOW + DocuSign (includes the ramp schedule and SLO language) for legal/ procurement review.
- Please confirm internal approval guardrails (signing authority & PO timing).
- Monica will coordinate the onboarding timeline and runbook.

If that sounds good I can send the DocuSign link today and loop finance for billing terms.

Thanks —
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
